title.zh: 卷24 列傳第16 盧辯
title.raw: 卷24 列傳第16 盧辯 Volume 24 Biographies 16: Lu Bian

translations.literal: Lu Bian, styled Jingxuan, was a native of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bian, styled Jingxuan, came from Zhuo in Fanyang commandery.

translations.literal: For generations his family had pursued Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His family had produced Confucian scholars for generations.

translations.literal: His father Jing was Assistant Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing served as Assistant Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 辯少好學，博通經籍，舉秀才，為太學博士。

translations.literal: From youth Bian loved learning, mastered the classics, was nominated as xiucai, and became Academician of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Bian loved learning from his youth, attained broad mastery of the classics, was nominated as a xiucai candidate, and was appointed Academician of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 以《大戴禮》未有解詁，辯乃注之。

translations.literal: Because the Record of Rites of the Elder Dai had no commentary, Bian thereupon annotated it.
translations.idiomatic: As the Record of Rites of the Elder Dai still lacked a commentary, Bian undertook to annotate it.

sentences.zh: 其兄景裕為當時碩儒，謂辯曰：「昔侍中注《小戴》，今爾注《大戴》，庶纂前修矣。」

translations.literal: His elder brother Jingyu was a leading scholar of the age and said to Bian: “In the past the Attendant-in-Chief annotated the Record of Rites of the Younger Dai; now you annotate the Elder Dai—you will carry on the work of your predecessors.”
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Jingyu, a leading scholar of the day, told Bian: “Long ago the Attendant-in-Chief annotated the Younger Dai’s Record of Rites; now you annotate the Elder Dai’s—you will be continuing the labors of those who came before.”

sentences.zh: 及帝入關，事起倉卒，辯不及至家，單馬而從。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered the Pass, affairs arose in sudden haste; Bian had no time to reach home and followed on horseback alone.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered the Pass, events erupted in sudden confusion. Bian had no time to go home and rode out alone to follow him.

translations.literal: Someone asked Bian: “Were you able to take leave of your family?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Bian: “Were you able to bid farewell to your household?”

sentences.zh: 」辯曰：「門外之治，以義斷恩，復何辭也。

translations.literal: ” Bian said: “In affairs outside the door, duty is decided by righteousness and severs private affection—what need is there to take leave?
translations.idiomatic: Bian replied: “In public affairs beyond the household, righteousness cuts through private ties—what farewell could there be?”

sentences.zh: 」孝武至長安，授給事黃門侍郎，領著作。

translations.literal: ” When Emperor Xiaowu reached Chang’an, [Bian] was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and concurrently Overseer of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu arrived at Chang’an, Bian was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and concurrently Overseer of Composition.

sentences.zh: 太祖以辯有儒術，甚禮之，朝廷大議，常召顧問。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke, seeing that Bian possessed Confucian learning, treated him with great courtesy; in major court deliberations he was regularly summoned for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Because Bian was steeped in Confucian learning, the Grand Duke treated him with great respect and regularly called on him for counsel in weighty court debates.

sentences.zh: 趙青雀之亂，魏太子出居渭北。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of Zhao Qingque, the Wei crown prince moved out to the north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhao Qingque’s rebellion, the Wei crown prince withdrew to the north bank of the Wei River.

translations.literal: Bian followed at the time and likewise did not inform his family.
translations.idiomatic: Bian accompanied him on that occasion as well, and again told no one at home.

translations.literal: His firmness of purpose and resolute decisions were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His steadfast resolve and decisive action were always of this kind.

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 魏太子及諸王等，皆行束修之禮，受業於辯。

translations.literal: The Wei crown prince and the various princes all performed the ceremony of dried-meat offering and received instruction from Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei crown prince and the other princes all presented the dried-meat gift of discipleship and studied under Bian.

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Duke of Fanyang and transferred to Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was ennobled as Duke of Fanyang and promoted to Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 自魏末離亂，孝武西遷，朝章禮度，湮墜咸盡。

translations.literal: From the disorders at the end of Wei, when Emperor Xiaowu moved west, court regulations and ritual forms were completely lost.
translations.idiomatic: After the chaos of the Wei’s final years, when Emperor Xiaowu moved the court westward, statutes and ritual observance collapsed entirely.

translations.literal: Bian adapted measures to the times, and all accorded with proper standards.
translations.idiomatic: Bian shaped institutions to fit the times, and in every case they matched the proper norms.

translations.literal: By nature he had a powerful memory and silent understanding, and could decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had an exceptionally retentive memory and an intuitive grasp of essentials, and could settle great matters of state.

translations.literal: Whatever institutions he established, he handled without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever systems he devised, he carried through without second thoughts.

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded, he was advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Bian was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與諸公幸其第，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited his residence with the various nobles—a glory for a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once came with the chief ministers to Bian’s house—an honor few scholars ever received.

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Governor of Yizhou.

translations.literal: When he died, he was granted paired sacrifice in the Grand Duke’s temple.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was granted the honor of paired offerings in the Grand Duke’s ancestral temple.

translations.literal: His son was Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son named Shen.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖欲行《周官》，命蘇綽專掌其事。

translations.literal: Initially the Grand Duke wished to implement the Offices of Zhou and ordered Su Chuo to take sole charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Grand Duke planned to put the Offices of Zhou into practice and put Su Chuo in sole charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 未幾而綽卒，乃令辯成之。

translations.literal: Before long Su Chuo died, and he then had Bian complete the work.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Su Chuo died, and the Grand Duke had Bian finish what he had begun.

sentences.zh: 於是依《周禮》建六官，置公、卿、大夫、士，並撰次朝儀，車服器用，多依古禮，革漢、魏之法。

translations.literal: Thereupon according to the Rites of Zhou they established the six ministries, set up dukes, ministers, grand masters, and officers, and compiled court ceremony, chariots, robes, and utensils—largely following ancient rites and replacing Han and Wei law.
translations.idiomatic: They then modeled the six ministries on the Rites of Zhou, appointed dukes, ministers, grand masters, and officers, and drew up court ritual, carriages, dress, and implements—largely reviving ancient forms and abolishing Han and Wei usage.

translations.literal: The matters were all put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: All of these measures were carried out.

sentences.zh: 今錄辯所述六官著之於篇。

translations.literal: Now the six ministries as set forth by Bian are recorded in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records the six ministries as Bian described them.

sentences.zh: 天官府管冢宰等衆職，地官府領司徒等衆職，春官府領宗伯等衆職，夏官府領司馬等衆職，秋官府領司寇等衆職，冬官府領司空等衆職。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Heaven oversaw the Chancellor of the Secretariat and other offices; the Ministry of Earth oversaw the Minister of Education and others; the Spring Ministry oversaw the Minister of Rites and others; the Summer Ministry the Minister of War; the Autumn Ministry the Minister of Justice; the Winter Ministry the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Heaven supervised the Chancellor of the Secretariat and the rest; Earth supervised the Minister of Education and the rest; Spring the Minister of Rites; Summer the Minister of War; Autumn the Minister of Justice; and Winter the Minister of Works.

translations.literal: The chronicle gives full details but the text is mostly not reproduced here.
translations.idiomatic: The annals contain fuller records, but most of the text is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 辯所述六官，太祖以魏恭帝三年始命行之。

translations.literal: The six ministries as set forth by Bian were first ordered implemented by the Grand Duke in the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Duke first ordered Bian’s six-ministry system into effect in the third year of Emperor Gong of Wei.

translations.literal: From that time onward, each generation made additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: After that, each reign revised the system with additions and cuts.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，事不師古，官員班品，隨意變革。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he did not take antiquity as his teacher; official titles and grades were altered at will.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, he no longer looked to antiquity for guidance; ranks and titles were changed as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 至如初置四輔官，及六府諸司復置中大夫，幷御正、內史增置上大夫等，則載於外史。

translations.literal: As for the initial establishment of the four auxiliary offices, and the restoration of middle grand masters in the six ministry offices together with additions of upper grand masters in the Office of the Imperial Clan and the Inner Scribe—these are recorded in the outer history.
translations.idiomatic: Matters such as the first creation of the four auxiliary posts, the reappointment of middle grand masters in the six ministries, and the addition of upper grand masters in the Office of the Imperial Clan and the Inner Scribe are recorded in the outer annals.

sentences.zh: 餘則朝出夕改，莫能詳錄。

translations.literal: The rest were changed morning and evening, and cannot be set down in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else was altered from day to day, and cannot be chronicled in full.

sentences.zh: 于時雖行《周禮》，其內外衆職，又兼用秦漢等官。

translations.literal: At that time although the Rites of Zhou were practiced, domestic and external offices also used Qin and Han titles concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Even while the Rites of Zhou were nominally in force, inner and outer offices still drew on Qin and Han titles side by side.

sentences.zh: 今略舉其名號及命數，附之于左。

translations.literal: Now titles and salary grades are briefly listed and appended at left.
translations.idiomatic: What follows is a brief list of titles and salary grades, set out on the left.

sentences.zh: 其紀傳內更有餘官而於此不載者，亦史闕文也。

translations.literal: If the biographies contain further offices not entered here, that too is where the history lacks text.
translations.idiomatic: Other offices mentioned in the biographies but omitted here likewise reflect gaps in the record.

translations.idiomatic: The above offices rank at the full three grades.

sentences.zh: 蕩寇、蕩難將軍，武騎常侍、侍郎，開府府參軍，驃騎車騎府、八命州列曹參軍，寧遠揚烈伏波輕車府長史，正六命州治中，六命郡丞，戶不滿五百以下縣令，戍主，正六命州呼藥。

translations.literal: Bandit-Sweeping and Hardship-Sweeping Generals; Martial Cavalry Regular Attendant and Vice Director; staff officers of a founding headquarters; staff officers of the various bureaus of the Fast Cavalry and Chariots and Cavalry headquarters in a province of the eight grades; chief clerk of the Far-Soothing, Glory-Raising, Wave-Quelling, and Light-Chariot headquarters; Chief Administrator of a province of the full six grades; Assistant Prefect of a commandery of the six grades; magistrates of counties with fewer than five hundred households; Garrison Chiefs; Huyao of a province of the full six grades.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit-Sweeping and Hardship-Sweeping Generals; Martial Cavalry Regular Attendant and Vice Director; staff officers of a founding headquarters; staff officers of the Fast Cavalry and Chariots and Cavalry headquarters in a province of the eight grades; chief clerks of the Far-Soothing, Glory-Raising, Wave-Quelling, and Light-Chariot headquarters; the Chief Administrator of a province of the full six grades; the Assistant Prefect of a commandery of the six grades; magistrates of counties with fewer than five hundred households; Garrison Chiefs; and the Huyao of a province of the full six grades.

translations.literal: Ranked at three grades on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The above offices rank at three grades.

sentences.zh: 殄寇、殄難將軍，強弩、〔積弩〕司馬，四征中鎮撫〔軍〕府、正七命州列曹參軍，正五命郡丞。

translations.literal: Bandit-Exterminating and Hardship-Exterminating Generals; Strong Crossbow and [Repeated Crossbow] Marshals; staff officers of the various bureaus of the Eastern, Western, Southern, and Northern Pacifying, Central Army, Army Suppressor, and Army Pacifier [Army] headquarters in a province of the full seven grades; Assistant Prefect of a commandery of the full five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit-Exterminating and Hardship-Exterminating Generals; Strong Crossbow and Repeated Crossbow Marshals; staff officers of the Pacifying, Central Army, Army Suppressor, and Army Pacifier headquarters in a province of the full seven grades; and the Assistant Prefect of a commandery of the full five grades.

translations.literal: Ranked at full two grades on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The above offices rank at the full two grades.

sentences.zh: 掃寇、掃難將軍，〔武騎〕、武威司馬，四平前後左右府、七命州列曹參軍，戍副，五命郡丞。

translations.literal: Bandit-Scouring and Hardship-Scouring Generals; [Martial Cavalry] and Martial Prestige Marshals; staff officers of the various bureaus of the Eastern, Western, Southern, and Northern Pacification, Front, Rear, Left, and Right headquarters in a province of the seven grades; Deputy Garrison Chiefs; Assistant Prefect of a commandery of the five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit-Scouring and Hardship-Scouring Generals; Martial Cavalry and Martial Prestige Marshals; staff officers of the Pacification, Front, Rear, Left, and Right headquarters in a province of the seven grades; Deputy Garrison Chiefs; and the Assistant Prefect of a commandery of the five grades.

translations.literal: Ranked at two grades on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The above offices rank at two grades.

sentences.zh: 曠野、橫野將軍，殿中、員外二司馬，冠軍輔國府、正六命州列曹參軍。

translations.literal: Wilderness and Transverse-Wilderness Generals; Palace and Supernumerary Second Marshals; staff officers of the various bureaus of the Champion and Assistant-State headquarters in a province of the full six grades.
translations.idiomatic: Wilderness and Transverse-Wilderness Generals; Palace and Supernumerary Second Marshals; and staff officers of the various bureaus of the Champion and Assistant-State headquarters in a province of the full six grades.

translations.literal: Ranked at full one grade on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The above offices rank at the full one grade.

sentences.zh: 威、武牙將軍，淮海、山林二都尉，鎮遠建忠中堅寧朔寧遠揚烈伏波輕車府列曹參軍。

translations.literal: Martial and Martial-Fang Generals; Huaihai and Mountain-Forest Commandants; staff officers of the various bureaus of the Far-Pacifying, Loyalty-Establishing, Stalwart, Northern-Soothing, Far-Soothing, Glory-Raising, Wave-Quelling, and Light-Chariot headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Martial and Martial-Fang Generals; the Huaihai and Mountain-Forest Commandants; and staff officers of the various bureaus of the Far-Pacifying, Loyalty-Establishing, Stalwart, Northern-Soothing, Far-Soothing, Glory-Raising, Wave-Quelling, and Light-Chariot headquarters.

translations.literal: Ranked at one grade on the right.
translations.idiomatic: The above offices rank at one grade.

sentences.zh: 周制：封郡縣五等爵者，皆加開國；

translations.literal: Under Zhou institutions: those enfeoffed with the five grades of nobility in commanderies and counties all received the addition “Founding State”;
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou practice: anyone enfeoffed with one of the five noble ranks in a commandery or county was also styled “Founder of the State”;

sentences.zh: 授柱國大將軍、開府、儀同者，並加使持節、大都督；

translations.literal: those granted the titles Grand Duke General of the Army, Founding Grand Commander, or Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies all received the additions Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Grand Commander-in-Chief;
translations.idiomatic: those appointed Grand Duke General of the Army, founding grand commander, or staff equal to the Three Excellencies were likewise given the titles Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Grand Commander-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 其開府又加〔驃騎大將軍、侍中；

translations.literal: for a founding headquarters, [Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Attendant-in-Chief were also added;
translations.idiomatic: a founding grand commander also received [the additional titles Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Attendant-in-Chief;

sentences.zh: 其儀同又加〕車騎大將軍、散騎常侍；

translations.literal: for staff equal to the Three Excellencies, ] Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Regular Palace Attendant were also added;
translations.idiomatic: while staff equal to the Three Excellencies also received ] Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Regular Palace Attendant;

sentences.zh: 其授總管刺史，則加使持節、諸軍事。

translations.literal: those appointed Area Commander or Governor received the additions Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander over All Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: those made Area Commander or Governor were given Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander over All Military Affairs.

translations.literal: This was the standing rule.
translations.idiomatic: These were the standing additions.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，詔總管刺史及行兵者，加持節，餘悉罷之。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Elephant reign era, an edict ordered that Area Commanders, Governors, and those leading troops on campaign should hold the staff of authority; all others were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Elephant era, an edict declared that only Area Commanders, Governors, and commanders in the field should bear the staff of authority; all other such titles were abolished.

sentences.zh: 建德四年，增置上柱國大將軍，改儀同三司為儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Jiande reign era, the post of Supreme Grand Duke General of the Army was added, and Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies was changed to Grand General with Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiande, the office of Supreme Grand Duke General of the Army was created, and “Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies” was renamed Grand General with Staff Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: The entire chapter has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou (November 1971).
